annotations.title: Check the whole app before deploying

description: Check how the app uses the chart library, before every deploy and after check_chart: reads the app's own source (never the files generate_chart and setup_fabric_app wrote) and reports, each with file, line and the library call to use instead: hand-written selection glue (a toggle, a second-click guard, a remount to clear) where useBicFilter + selects does it; each chart's filter wiring - the page filter its clicks set and the filters its query or component follows (filtered query, highlight only or none) - with a chart filtered by the filter it sets, a treatAs column the model's relationships can't carry to the panel, or to one of its measures (read from the tables each measure's expression reads) (read from the project's schema cache, .schema/models/*/model.sqlite), a total that isn't the sum of the parts the page shows (a rounding measure at the total), a click filter keyed coarser than the marks that set it, a chart carrying write markers whose query drops rows the write form can target, several charts sharing one click filter, a chart no page filter reaches, and a panel whose filtered query it isn't given; a "vs" measure in the app's .dax queries that is never blank (BLANK() - 1 is -1), a card that names a window ("2019 to 2025") over a query with no bound on it, and a query a line over time reads that can drop a quiet period (SUMMARIZECOLUMNS with no COALESCE or ADDMISSINGITEMS), a query whose range is a date written in (DATE ( y, m, d )) where it should come from the data or the person's words; a write that stores a placeholder name ("unknown") when no one is signed in or a time from the browser's clock, a Rayfin entity that takes any name on create or lets any row be updated again (rayfin/data), a name shown (createdBy) its policy doesn't check against the caller's token, a function that reads the caller's email from preferred_username or upn (Rayfin reads only the email claim), a write that resolves before its reload lands (so its button comes back on over the old rows), reloads applied out of order, a list that can't tell loading from empty, a form default read once, a due date with no lower bound, a due date the server refuses by UTC's today (or its own) while the form's min is the reader's date, a read of every row on every open, a panel with no Retry, a write that only a chart pick can aim (no searchable picker), a list for a picked owner filtered on another owner field than the form saves, a sign-in check weaker than the save's, a lookup whose rows feed the page while its loading and failure show only in a dialog, a blank value put into text with String() ("null"), saved rows never reloaded when the page comes back into view, a done-once write that reloads only on success, a dialog list copied into state when it opened, and a dialog that doesn't hold the keyboard; light and dark: no light/dark toggle, the template's theme hook (it flips a reader's pick back), a color written as a literal where a theme token belongs, and a dialog scrim that washes the page in one theme; a card's static text that states an order the reader can change ("highest first"); a page filter read as its first key only (`.value`), where a group pick holds several; row positions read from the DOM; the payload's __rowIdx__ / __geo* columns built by hand; a slider beside a chart that draws its own controls (useBicControls); notes kept but never shown on the marks (annotations); a chart outside a BicChartPanel, a fixed height below the panel's minimum, a fixed card height whose title and subtitle (wrapped at a phone's width) leave its chart under its minimum, a minChartWidth wider than a phone gives a chart (294px) and than the chart type's own minimum, a chart's card narrower than its chart's minimum at any page width from 1024 to 1920px (worked out from the page's grid), a flex-1 container without min-h-0 / min-w-0; two charts setting the same element id; a chart that judges a measure good or bad but was generated with no direction of good; an installed @bicharts/chart-host older than the generated components need (0.6.86); and @bicharts / Rayfin / Fabric visuals packages behind npm's latest. It also draws every chart under src/charts the way check_chart does and reports any that throw, come out blank or don't pass a click to onSelect. Local and free; npm is only asked for versions, and a stack finding is skipped when npm can't be reached. Layout findings are WARNINGS: a static read can't prove a layout. Fix the app's own files; regenerate a chart rather than edit its generated code.

check_npm.description: Compare the stack with npm's latest (default true).

draw_charts.description: Also draw every chart under src/charts (default true).

project_dir.description: The app's folder. Defaults to the folder setup_fabric_app used, else the working directory or the one project folder inside it.
